title: The little singing whale
summary: Lía never sings, because her voice is thin and ends in a squeak. Until she gets lost at sea, where whales can only find each other by singing.

scenes.text:
Lía was the smallest whale in her family, and she never let out a single note.

The others did. Every evening, when the sun went down and the sea turned dark blue, the big whales began their songs. Their voices were deep and long, like huge doors opening slowly at the bottom of the sea.

Lía had tried once, when she was very little.

Out of her mouth came a thin thread of a voice, wobbly and crooked, that ended in a squeak.

A passing fish laughed so hard that all its bubbles escaped.

From that day on, Lía listened to the others with her mouth shut tight.

One day, the family set off on the long journey north, where the water is cold and full of food.

Lía swam at the back, as always. And as always, everything distracted her.

A shoal of silver fish that kept changing shape. A sunken ship, all covered in seaweed, where a very grumpy crab lived. A jellyfish that lit up and went dark again like a little lantern.

She stopped to watch the jellyfish for a moment.

Just a moment.

When she looked up, the sea was empty.

No big tails ahead. No shadows. Only blue water above, below and on every side.

"Mama!" called Lía.

But her voice was so small that the water swallowed it at once.

She waited. She swam one way, and then the other. Everything looked the same everywhere.

Then, very far away, she heard the big whales. They were singing, as they did every evening, to find each other in the enormous sea. Their deep voices came from everywhere at once: from above, from below, from nowhere at all.

Lía knew what she had to do. That is how whales find each other: by singing.

And she also knew she didn't want to. Her voice was thin. It was crooked. It ended in a squeak.

Her heart felt very small.

But she was alone, and the sea was very big, and night was coming.

So Lía closed her eyes, filled her lungs with air, and sang.

It came out the same as always: thin, crooked, with a squeak at the end.

She did it again. And again.

And then something strange happened. The deep voices, far away, all went quiet at once.

Silence.

Lía stopped, frightened. Had she done something wrong?

And out of the silence came a voice she knew better than any other. It was her mother. And she wasn't singing her usual deep song.

She was singing Lía's. Thin, crooked, with a squeak at the end.

Her mother came swimming so fast that she stirred up swirls.

She wrapped Lía in her flipper, and the two of them stayed very still, very close, while the rest of the family appeared out of the dark one by one.

"How did you find me?" asked Lía. "The voices were coming from everywhere."

"The big voices, yes," said her mother. "They all sound alike. But yours doesn't sound like anyone else's. I heard it from the other side of the sea."

Together, slowly, they rose to breathe at the surface.

That night, when the big whales began their songs, a thin and crooked voice joined in.

Nobody laughed. And when it ended in a squeak, that was everyone's favourite part.
